name: Skin Lesion Morphology and Bedside Diagnosis

reference.source: Neena Khanna Dermatology topic map + Fitzpatrick 8ed depth reference (text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Primary lesions name the process while secondary lesions record its evolution
Size cutoffs separate macule-patch and papule-plaque and vesicle-bulla
Distribution and pattern narrow the differential before tests
Bedside tests prove infection, blister level and pigment change

Pattern reading: annular active edges suggest tinea, extensor silvery plaques suggest psoriasis, flexural lichenification suggests atopic eczema, violaceous polygons suggest lichen planus, grouped vesicles suggest herpes, palmoplantar papules demand syphilis serology
Bedside proof: Wood lamp fluorescence, KOH mount for hyphae, Tzanck smear for giant or acantholytic cells, dermoscopy vessels, patch test for contact allergy
Sampling: edge punch for blister level, perilesional skin for direct immunofluorescence, slit smear for leprosy bacilli
reference.pathophysiology: Primary lesions arise directly from disease while secondary lesions follow scratching, healing or treatment. Flat colour change under about one centimetre is a macule and above it a patch; raised solid lesions under one centimetre are papules and broader flat-topped ones plaques; deep palpable lumps are nodules. Fluid blisters under half a centimetre are vesicles and larger ones bullae; pus-filled ones are pustules and transient oedematous ones wheals. Surface change gives scale, dried exudate gives crust, scratch marks give excoriation, chronic rubbing gives lichenification, and loss gives erosion above the basement zone versus ulcer below it.
additionalDifferentials: Psoriasis versus eczema versus lichen planus by scale, site and striae
Tinea versus pityriasis rosea versus granuloma annulare by edge activity
Pemphigus versus pemphigoid versus dermatitis herpetiformis by tension and mucosae
Impetigo versus herpes versus wart by crust, vesicle grouping and dots
additionalInvestigations: Potassium hydroxide mount with Wood lamp examination
Tzanck smear with punch biopsy and direct immunofluorescence
